authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: No generic Grixis combo shell; close through counter/sacrifice loops (decisions L16).
Cut Village Rites, Black Market Connections and others for loop and tutor density (decisions swaps).

blueprint_failure_modes.description: Exile removal and graveyard hate stop persist and Marchesa returns.
Losing Marchesa removes dethrone and recursion.
Counter removal or -1/-1 effects disrupt the resets.

value.interaction: Fierce Guardianship, Flare of Denial, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Toxic Deluge, Blasphemous Act, Cyclonic Rift.
value.mana: Sol Ring, Ancient Tomb, Talismans, sacrifice mana.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Marchesa gives the team dethrone and returns any countered creature that dies, which makes the sacrifice engine resilient.
accepted_role.honest_note: The source calls the closes 'commander-native loops' (decisions L16), but none of the 48 Spellbook infinites in the list needs Marchesa: they're persist/undying loops with Thran Vigil, Metallic Mimic, Gev, Uncivil Unrest or Mikaeus plus an outlet. She's a resilience engine, not the kill. The cycle 51 M1 review (marchbr-01..11, all verified) confirms the persist-reset loops.
